partner_applied.source: account04/B14 r6 fixed four-coordinate affine-core theorem
partner_applied.actual_application: After compressing the entire aligned V-bank to Y=(sqrt(2)/||a||)a^T V, the resulting four-variable active matrix has three eigenvalues bounded below at the explicit scale; the partner theorem is applied uniformly in the outside-generated affine terms.

newest_source_applied.actual_application: Used as the compatible diffuse-volume exit: under its M=M0+E leverage and operator-error gate, the ambient density is continuous and <23/a; the new theorem supplies a separate aligned rank-one exit.

proved.statement_summary: For A=[[B,k a^T,C],[a k^T,theta a a^T,a b^T],[C^T,b a^T,D]] in original coordinates with Bk=0 and a!=0, if both eigenvalues of B|k^perp have modulus >=nu, then ||p_Q||inf <= C4/min(nu,||a||/sqrt(2)), C4=1000(8+log4), uniformly for all theta, outside couplings, translations and cap-one rough product laws. If only one B eigenvalue is >=nu, replace ||a||/sqrt(2) by the exact smaller modulus delta(theta,r) of [[0,r],[r,theta r^2]].

stress_family: B=diag(1,-1,0), k=e3, a_N=sqrt(2/N)(1,...,1), arbitrary theta. The exact target spectral hypothesis holds for every N and theta while every individual leakage coefficient tends to zero; the theorem gives the uniform bound C4.
remaining_implication: Handle low-rank/high-leverage banks whose within-bank quadratic curvature or outside couplings are not aligned with the leakage direction. A successor must compress a small joint bank image or use an aggregate curved-kernel argument without destroying original product provenance.
next_step: Develop a two- or few-statistic bank compression theorem with a dimension-free joint density/curved estimate, while routing diffuse rank-at-least-three cross blocks through the c2414 volume-stability exit.
